links.title: Automate the Boring Stuff with Python, 3rd edition: Chapter 18, CSV, JSON, and XML Files
links.why: The course textbook's own chapter, free online: CSV reader and writer, Project 13, JSON and XML, with the practice questions.

links.title: csv — CSV File Reading and Writing
links.why: Every reader and writer option: dialects, quoting modes, DictReader and DictWriter, line_num and the newline='' rule.

links.title: json — JSON encoder and decoder
links.why: The conversion tables, default and indent, the standard-compliance notes and the python -m json command line.

links.title: xml.etree.ElementTree — The ElementTree XML API
links.why: Parsing, finding, building and writing XML, the XPath subset, iterparse and the Element truth-value warning.

links.title: XML Processing Modules
links.why: The modules of the xml package and the XML security section: entity expansion attacks and untrusted data.

links.title: tomllib — Parse TOML files
links.why: Reading TOML, the conversion table, and the fact that the module cannot write.

links.title: 7. Input and Output
links.why: The tutorial's section on saving structured data with json, including the UTF-8 note.

links.title: PEP 305 – CSV File API
links.why: Why the csv module exists: parsing lines by hand with split is bound to fail.

links.title: RFC 4180: Common Format and MIME Type for Comma-Separated Values (CSV) Files
links.why: The informal definition of CSV: CRLF line breaks, quoting of commas, quotes and line breaks, the optional header line.
